native_result.query: In the PCA on the forms of capital analyzed in hundred-year time slices, during the Younger Bronze Age (1100-500 BCE), how does the principal component value of PC1 in the beginning of the period at 1100 BCE differ from the subsequent time horizons between 1000 to 500 BCE?
native_result.HypoA: The beginning of the Younger Bronze Age (1100 BCE) is associated with negative values on the first principal component (PC1), while the majority of time horizons (1000-500 BCE) are characterized by positive values on PC1. This Principal component analysis (PCA) is on the forms of capital. The values of the individual elements of the forms of capital form the attributes.
native_result.HypoB: In the PCA on the 12 forms of capital (HatchetSword, Dagger, HouseSize, CopperGold, Amber, MonumentCount, Depot, Sickle, Axes&Celts, MonumentSize, PotteryForm, PotteryDecoration) computed per 100-year time slice over the Younger Bronze Age (1100-500 BCE), the PC1 score at the start of the period (BCE 1100) lies outside the [min, max] range of the six subsequent BCE 1000-500 horizons, on the side away from the central tendency of those later bins - i.e. PC1(1100) is the single most extreme economic-capital-positive reading of the Younger Bronze Age, and the magnitude of the gap (|PC1(1100) - PC1(t)|) tends to grow from BCE 1000 to BCE 500 (with a small local contraction at BCE 800). In the PCA-full run (fit on all 39 rows x 12 capital Z-features, projected to 7 YBA rows), PC1(1100) = -4.51 versus subsequent range [-2.18, -0.79]; in the PCA-YBA-only run (fit on 7 rows x 10 features after dropping ZSichel and ZKeform as zero-variance), PC1(1100) = +5.78 versus [-2.27, -0.03]; sign-flip rule kept the loadings of PC1 on ZCU_AU, ZAmber, ZHort and Zhausgr positively aligned. The Belau pollen openness score (Feeser et al. 2019), where available (BCE 1100-700), is positively correlated with PC1_full (r = +0.69) and negatively with PC1_ybaonly (r = -0.60); this is supporting context, not a PCA feature, and pollen data do not exist for BCE 600 and 500.
native_result.WorkflowB: Loaded capital.csv and pollen_openness_score_Belau_Woserin_Feeser_et_al_2019.csv with decimal=','. (a) PCA-full: fit SVD on the 39x12 globally-Z-standardised matrix (no zero-variance columns at full scale) and projected the 7 YBA rows through that rotation (raw PC1 variance ratio 0.3033). (b) PCA-YBA-only: filtered YBA rows, dropped ZSichel and ZKeform (zero variance within YBA), re-standardised on the 7x10 matrix, SVD fit (PC1 variance ratio 0.6253). For both runs, the same sign-flip rule was applied: keep PC1 sign unflipped only when loadings on {ZCU_AU, ZAmber, ZHort, Zhausgr} are all positive; otherwise negate PC1. PCA-YBA-only satisfied the rule directly; PCA-full required a single flip. Score tables and PC1(1100) - PC1(t) diff tables were written for both. Verdict: PC1(1100) is OUTSIDE the [min, max] of {PC1(1000..500)} in both runs - BELOW in PCA-full, ABOVE in PCA-YBA-only, both on the economic-capital-positive side. Pollen context: Belau_PC1_inter centroid mean per YBA bin was correlated with PC1 at the 5 overlapping horizons BCE 1100..700; BCE 600 and 500 acknowledged as missing. All artefacts written under /workspace/artifacts; executed analysis at /workspace/scripts/pca_analysis.py.
